verses.text: So there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who live by the Spirit instead of by their human nature.
The Spirit's law of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death.
The law couldn't free us because our human nature made it powerless. So God did: he sent his own Son in a human life like ours, to deal with sin, and condemned sin in that human life.
He did this so the law's just requirement could be fulfilled in us, as we live by the Spirit and not by our human nature.
Those who live by their human nature focus on what that nature wants. Those who live by the Spirit focus on what the Spirit wants.
A mind set on human nature leads to death, but a mind set on the Spirit brings life and peace.
A mind set on human nature is hostile to God. It doesn't submit to God's law—in fact, it can't.
Those who live by their human nature can't please God.
But you aren't living by your human nature; you're living by the Spirit, if God's Spirit truly lives in you. Anyone who doesn't have the Spirit of Christ doesn't belong to him.
If Christ is in you, your body is subject to death because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.
If the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, the one who raised Christ Jesus will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit living in you.
So then, brothers and sisters, we owe nothing to our human nature that would make us live by it.
If you live by your human nature, you'll die. But if by the Spirit you put the body's deeds to death, you'll live.
All who are led by God's Spirit are God's children.
You didn't receive a spirit of slavery that pulls you back into fear. You received the Spirit who makes you God's adopted children, and by him we cry, ‘Abba, Father!’
The Spirit himself confirms to our spirit that we are God's children.
And if we're children, we're heirs too—heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if we share his suffering so we can also share his glory.
I consider that what we suffer now can't compare with the glory that will soon be revealed to us.
All creation waits with eager expectation for God's children to be revealed.
Creation was made subject to frustration, not by its own choice but by the one who subjected it, in the hope
that creation itself will be set free from slavery to decay and share in the glorious freedom of God's children.
We know that all creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth right up to now.
And not only creation—we who have the first taste of the Spirit groan inwardly too as we wait for God to adopt us fully and redeem our bodies.
We were saved in this hope. But if we can already see what we hope for, that's not hope—who hopes for what they already see?
But if we hope for what we don't see, we wait for it with patience.
In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We don't know what we should pray for, but the Spirit himself pleads for us with groans too deep for words.
The one who searches our hearts knows what the Spirit intends, because the Spirit pleads for God's people in line with God's will.
We know that God works all things together for good for those who love him and are called according to his purpose.
Those he knew beforehand, he also chose beforehand to be shaped into the likeness of his Son, so that the Son would be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
Those he chose beforehand, he also called; those he called, he also made right; and those he made right, he also glorified.
So what can we say about all this? If God is for us, who can stand against us?
God didn't spare his own Son but gave him up for us all. Won't he also, along with him, freely give us everything we need?
Who can bring a charge against God's chosen people? God is the one who makes them right.
Who can condemn us? Christ Jesus is the one who died—and more than that, who was raised. He's at God's right hand, and he's also pleading for us.
Who can separate us from Christ's love? Trouble, hardship, persecution, hunger, poverty, danger, or violence?
As Scripture says, ‘For your sake we're being killed all day long; we're treated like sheep headed for slaughter.’
No! In all these things we have complete victory through the one who loved us.
I'm convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither what is happening now nor what is coming, nor any powers,
neither height nor depth nor anything else in all creation can separate us from God's love in Christ Jesus our Lord.
